phases.name: Model benchmarking
phases.notes: Independently re-verified live in this session (not just re-asserted): candidate isot-svm-37fc02617260 trained via scripts/train_isot_canonical.py on the real, SHA-256-verified ISOT release assets. test F1=0.9962, temporal_test F1=0.9988, validation F1=0.9949 (Linear SVM, Platt-calibrated). artifact_sha256 in the manifest verified to match the real artifact file. production artifact confirmed byte-identical to main throughout (untouched).

phases.name: Proper calibration
phases.notes: Calibrated Linear SVM was evaluated with Brier score and 10-bin expected calibration error on real ISOT. Cross-domain calibration/generalization still needs external validation.

phases.name: Model versioning
phases.notes: Canonical training, versioned candidates, dataset fingerprinting, LIAR candidate validation, and explicit promotion/rollback tooling exist on ml-upgrade-phase9-model-versioning (PR #12) and were independently exercised live end-to-end in this session: prepare -> train -> validate -> temporal test -> LIAR external validation -> candidate artifact, all producing real, freshly-computed results (see docs/PHASE9_MODEL_GOVERNANCE.md for exact numbers). Governance test suite (backend/tests/test_phase9_model_governance.py) was found with 1 real failure (wording mismatch between promote_model.py's unconditional blocking message and the test's assertion for the literal word 'required'), root-caused, fixed by making both blocking messages in promote_model.py consistent (no safety weakening), and re-verified 3/3 passing. A separately-identified dead/unreachable secondary approval check was documented in place (kept as defense-in-depth) rather than silently left unexplained. Production artifact (data/saved_model_artifacts.json) confirmed byte-identical to main (SHA-256 match) -- no automatic promotion occurred or is possible without the explicit --approve AND --yes flags, which promote_model.py enforces unconditionally before touching production.

phases.name: Production runtime audit (server/mlEngine.ts, /api/health)
phases.notes: Found and fixed a real bug: the constructor checked file existence but never checked loadModelArtifact()'s return value, so a present-but-corrupt/inconsistent artifact left the engine with an empty vocabulary forever (every prediction silently exactly P(FAKE)=0.5, always landing in the uncertainty zone, with /api/health still hardcoded to 'ok'). Fixed: constructor now falls back to train() whenever loadModelArtifact() returns false, matching the missing-file behavior. Added isModelTrained() and an additive, backward-compatible model_trained field + status:'degraded' case on /api/health. Verified live with an intentionally corrupted artifact on a running server. Added scripts/test_artifact_lifecycle.ts (9/9 passing) covering valid/missing/corrupt/inconsistent/empty-vocab artifacts via a new artifactFileOverride constructor parameter (isolated temp dirs only, never touches the real production file). No regressions: regressionVerdictTests.ts 28/28, adversarialAcceptanceTests.ts 24/25 (the one failure requires GEMINI_API_KEY, confirmed pre-existing/environmental, unrelated to this change). Production artifact confirmed byte-identical (SHA-256) throughout. FOLLOW-UP (same session): the initial fix's fallback called train(), which unconditionally persisted to disk -- meaning merely importing the module or calling getDiagnostics()/getMetrics() could silently overwrite the real production artifact, bypassing Phase 9's explicit-promotion-only governance. Fixed with a persist parameter on train() (default true, unchanged for the 3 genuinely explicit human call sites: POST /api/train, POST /api/dataset/reset-demo, dataset-import; false for all implicit/lazy fallback call sites). Also found and fixed a related crash: getDiagnostics()/getMetrics() only checked this.metrics for truthiness, not shape, so a present-but-incomplete metrics object (missing best_model) crashed with an unhandled TypeError. Regression suite now 12/12 (was 9/9), including two new tests that byte-compare the corrupt-artifact file and the real production artifact before/after exercising the engine. Hash-guarded verification around every test run in this session (new suite, regressionVerdictTests.ts 28/28, adversarialAcceptanceTests.ts 24/25) showed zero production artifact change throughout.
